title: Genotype-phenotype map for the flying-fish blueprint, from proxy fish, at every layer
constraint: Almost no molecular data exists for flying fish (Exocoetidae). NCBI holds one scaffold-level assembly (GCA_018398805.1, Hirundichthys speculiger) and OrthoDB holds no genome for the whole suborder Belonoidei. Every gene link here was measured in a PROXY species, zebrafish (Danio rerio) or medaka (Oryzias latipes, same order Beloniformes as flying fish). None of it is flying-fish data.
causation_warning: Most links are 'expressed in': the gene's RNA or protein was detected in the structure. That is not causation. 'required for' means a single-gene loss-of-function zebrafish has an abnormal phenotype there (or, for GO-based links, that GO places the gene in the structure's developmental process on mutant evidence). 'sufficient for' here means a verified gain-of-function allele changes the structure (e.g. enlarges it); it does not mean the gene makes the structure. No gene 'makes' a fin.

propagation_rules.expressed in: propagates UP part_of: expression in a part implies some expression in what contains it. Marked derived with the path.
propagation_rules.required for: never propagates DOWN. Propagation UP is an inference, marked derived, never presented as observed.
propagation_rules.graph: the blueprint's own part_of placements (organism-design/examples/a-flying-fish.json), which the lean thread kernel-certified as acyclic and rooted, so propagation is well defined and terminates. Bgee's own propagation is excluded: only Bgee calls that include data observed in that very structure are used.

blueprint.pectoral_fin_note: In the blueprint the pectoral fin has one tissue beneath it (mesenchyme pectoral fin) and no cell types. ZFA has 52 terms that are parts of the zebrafish pectoral fin; the blueprint has a node for none of them except the mesenchyme, so ZFIN records on those parts do not attach.

gene_breadth.note: how many blueprint nodes each gene touches by direct record; a gene in many nodes is pleiotropic, not a fin gene

gene_id_rules.note: Bgee 15.2 and ZFIN's ensembl_1_to_1 table use different Ensembl releases. A Bgee gene whose Ensembl id is absent from ZFIN's table is merged onto the ZFIN gene with exactly the same symbol; otherwise it keeps its Ensembl id as its key. Medaka genes keep Ensembl ids (no ZFIN).

gaps: No ezh2 data in a flying fish (Exocoetidae).
No cellular or molecular measurement in the ezh2 mutant pectoral fin or fin bud in any paper fetched; the fin phenotype is scored by gross morphology only.

No fin-specific experiment: MZezh2 is a global maternal-zygotic null, the authors state their experiments were on whole embryos, and the mRNA rescue is global and was scored on eyes and circulation rather than fins. The fin phenotype in this mutant should be treated as indirect.
The ezh2 mutant dies at 2 dpf, so no evidence can exist for fin subparts (girdle, radials, lepidotrichia) or for the adult enlarged-fin phenotype the project cares about.

A separate ezh2 line is reported to fail caudal fin regeneration (PMID 28887218, abstract only); that is the caudal fin, not the pectoral fin, and was not used here.

sources.quote: Zebrafish embryos homozygous for jellyfish (jef) mutations show craniofacial defects and lack cartilage elements of the neurocranium, pharyngeal arches, and pectoral girdle similar to humans with campomelic dysplasia.
Distinct subsets of the craniofacial skeleton, otic placode and pectoral appendage express each gene, and are defective in each single mutant.
These mutants also exhibit shortened heads and reduced pectoral fins.
